description:
Somos un equipo multidisciplinario de Bolivia, con estudiantes de ingeniería de sistemas, ingeniería industrial y bioingeniería, y trabajaremos en “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Queremos usar datos de la NASA para ayudar a los agricultores a adaptarse a los cambios del clima y crear una herramienta con impacto real.

Buscamos personas con habilidades en análisis de datos, SIG/teledetección, agronomía, o diseño y edición de video. ¡Todos los niveles son bienvenidos!
details:
What it does. Raíz is a decision-support tool for one pilot area: Obrajes, Soracachi, Oruro, Bolivia. It compares three crop rotations taken from a local farmer's calendar:

  • potato → quinoa → fallow;
  • potato → quinoa → faba bean;
  • potato → faba bean → fallow.

Each rotation is evaluated in its 3 cyclic starting positions, giving 9 cases, so the El Niño / La Niña / Neutral "decision season" falls on each crop. Results are shown for that season and for the full 3-season cycle.

How it works.

  1. We downloaded NASA POWER daily data (1981–2026) for the point and classified each November–March season with NOAA's Oceanic Niño Index (NDJ).
    • net irrigation requirement;
    • water-stress days;
    • frost exposure during flowering (crop-specific thresholds);
    • bare-soil exposure to heavy rain and wind;
    • planned soil cover.
  2. Results are precomputed and validated against a strict data contract. No live calls to providers happen during use.
  3. The same results feed a web comparator, printable sheets for technicians, and a regional radio-ready bulletin.

Local evidence. A farmer in Obrajes described his practice: well irrigation for potato and faba bean, rain-fed quinoa, and fallow grazed by neighbours' animals. He named his main losses: frost during flowering and hail. He recorded the Quechua bulletin with written consent. His exact location is not published (point rounded to 0.01°).

Why it matters. Climate alerts say "El Niño is coming" but do not answer the farmer's real question: what should be in each plot this year, and how much well water will it need?

Honest limits. The data is regional (~50 km NASA POWER cell), not plot-level. The strong El Niño sample is n = 5, so we report a historical frequency, not a probability. Hail is not measured. Soil is estimated from texture, not measured. A second rainfall source (CHIRPS/IMERG/SENAMHI) was not available in time, so source sensitivity is reported as "not evaluated".

Tools. Python (pandas, NumPy), FastAPI, React/Vite, Meta MMS-TTS (CC-BY-NC-4.0) for the Spanish synthetic voice.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources), Daily API, AG community, 1981–2026. Variables: PRECTOTCORR, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, WS2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN. Use: seasonal rainfall, ET0, water balance, frost exposure.
NASADEM elevation (3,809 m at the pilot point).
